problem: LLMs deployed in user-facing applications exhibit persistent biases that disadvantage or stereotype certain groups, but existing bias benchmarks fail to capture real-world complexity.
approach: A counterfactual framework automatically generates realistic, open-ended questions that systematically explore areas where models exhibit biased behavior through iterative question mutation, capturing nuanced response dimensions like asymmetric refusals.
contribution: Introduces CAB, a diverse human-verified benchmark showing that all examined frontier LLMs persist in exhibiting biases across various scenarios.

problem: Long-horizon forecasting requires learning accurate spectral structure of local Jacobians, not only matching conditional means, but standard methods lack explicit spectral modeling.
approach: Fern uses Brenier's theorem to directly parameterize the Jacobian as symmetric positive semi-definite factorization, treating forecasting as optimal transport of probability mass to data-dependent ellipsoids, enabling efficient orthogonal factors and interpretable diagnostics.
contribution: Demonstrates exceptional stability on nonstationary settings, outperforming baselines by up to 790× where standard benchmarks fail to expose brittleness.

problem: Common visual anomaly detection evaluation metrics fail to capture practically relevant model behavior and yield inconsistent assessments by overlooking errors like redundant detections and spatial false positive distribution.
approach: Formalizes VAD evaluation through axiomatic properties that metrics should satisfy, showing existing methods fail these properties, then introduces SAAM-ALARM as a metric satisfying all properties.
contribution: Establishes SAAM-ALARM as a theoretically sound evaluation metric providing more nuanced performance assessment and stronger benchmarking standard.

problem: The Gilbert-Pollak Conjecture on Steiner ratio has stalled at a lower bound of 0.824 for three decades despite intense effort, and LLMs' potential for advancing research-level mathematical problems remains underexplored.
approach: An AI system tasks LLMs with generating rule-constrained geometric lemmas as executable code, using these to construct verification functions that yield certified lower bounds through progressive lemma refinement driven by reflection.
contribution: Establishes a new certified lower bound of 0.8559 for the Steiner ratio using only thousands of LLM calls, demonstrating LLM-based systems' potential for advanced mathematical research.

problem: Distinguishing whether language models genuinely reason or merely pattern-match remains open, and existing verification methods are either expensive or brittle.
approach: Treats each attention matrix as a weighted token graph and extracts four training-free spectral diagnostics (Fiedler value, HFER, spectral entropy, smoothness) to classify valid mathematical reasoning with 85-96% accuracy.
contribution: Reveals measurable spectral signatures in transformer attention that track logical coherence with effect sizes up to Cohen's d=3.30, and reranking with HFER improves proof search by 4.4-6.6%.

problem: Learning from long-tailed noisy data compounds two challenges, and existing methods ignore the non-uniform noise impact across classes, causing ineffective tail correction and over-regularization of head classes.
approach: CARE uses vision-language models to leverage three supervision sources (noisy labels, VLM text embeddings, visual features) with class-adaptive expert consensus that enforces stricter agreement for tail classes and permissive agreement for head classes.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.0% performance gains on both synthetic and real-world benchmarks by recalibrating class distributions more reliably.

problem: Unified hyperspectral image restoration across diverse degradations requires capturing multi-dimensional degradations, but current methods rely on impractical priors or black-box representations that overfit and fail on unseen scenarios.
approach: DAMP characterizes degradations through interpretable spatial-spectral metrics as Degradation Prompts, using Degradation-Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts with Spatial-Spectral Adaptive Modules that dynamically activate experts tailored to specific degradation profiles.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on natural and remote sensing datasets with exceptional zero-shot generalization to unseen restoration tasks.

problem: Test-time adaptation reduces error on new data but model parameters become dependent on past test inputs, raising privacy risks from memorizing sensitive testing data.
approach: Casts multiple TTA methods (Tent, EATA, SAR, DeYO, COME) into differential privacy forms using per-sample gradient clipping and Gaussian noise for all updates.
contribution: Provides adequate privacy at small accuracy cost on ImageNet-C, where low-privacy regimes even improve accuracy and stability of continual adaptation.

problem: Post-training LLM preference alignment requires access to sensitive user preference data, raising privacy concerns about dataset exposure.
approach: DPPrefSyn learns an underlying preference model from private data with formal differential privacy guarantees grounded in Bradley-Terry preference model, then synthesizes high-quality preference data using learned models and public prompts via DP-PCA.
contribution: Achieves competitive alignment performance under strong differential privacy guarantees, demonstrating synthetic preference data as a practical privacy-preserving alternative.

problem: Rank estimation under label noise requires handling structured ordinal label uncertainty rather than simple corruption, and existing methods fail to capture this.
approach: Reformulates rank estimation as a stochastic ordering problem where instances have multiple plausible ranks, using discriminative loss for instance-centroid interactions and stochastic order loss for probabilistic ordering relations.
contribution: Enables reliable rank estimation across diverse datasets under various types and levels of label noise.

problem: One-step and few-step flow-based generation requires enforcing long-range trajectory consistency, but directly supervising this over long time scales is difficult.
approach: Euler Mean Flows replace the trajectory consistency constraint with a principled linear surrogate derived from the semigroup formulation, enabling direct data supervision and supporting both u-prediction and x_1-prediction variants without explicit Jacobian computation.
contribution: Achieves improved optimization stability and sample quality with approximately 50% reductions in training time and memory compared to existing one-step methods.

problem: Time-series forecasting progress is obscured by complex architectures and fragile, misattributed gains, hindering meaningful comparison and understanding of what drives performance.
approach: CombinationTS decomposes forecasting models into orthogonal modules (Input Transformation, Embedding, Encoder, Decoder, Output Transformation) and evaluates under shared conditions with marginalized performance and stability metrics.
contribution: Reveals the Identity Paradox: well-designed data embedding often matches or outperforms complex backbones, enabling robust component attribution.

problem: Standard reward models in RLHF are susceptible to spurious features unrelated to human labels, leading to reward hacking where high predicted reward fails to translate to better behavior.
approach: Proposes factored representation learning that decomposes contextual embeddings into causal factors sufficient for reward prediction and non-causal factors capturing length/sycophancy, with adversarial training via gradient reversal on non-causal components.
contribution: Learns more robust reward models and consistently improves downstream RLHF performance while mitigating reward hacking on both mathematical and dialogue tasks.

problem: Machine unlearning typically requires modifying model parameters, but such updates are unstable, computationally costly, and limited by local approximations.
approach: Representation Unlearning learns a transformation in the model's representation space imposing an information bottleneck that maximizes mutual information with retained data while suppressing information about forgotten data, using variational surrogates.
contribution: Achieves more reliable forgetting, better utility retention, and greater computational efficiency than parameter-centric approaches in both zero-shot and full-data settings.

problem: LIME provides unfaithful and unstable explanations for tabular data when local feature effects exhibit nonlinear or heterogeneous behaviors, and relies on decoupled feature selection misaligned with the objective.
approach: PL-LIME models feature-wise local effects using instance-anchored piecewise linear functions under a fixed budget, with decoupled nonnegative shrinkage that directly scales estimated effects while preserving interpretability.
contribution: Achieves higher local fidelity and stability with more reliable explanations capturing finer-grained local effect structures than LIME.

problem: Vision foundation models fail to exploit 3D structure cues in 2D images, underperforming on tasks like multiview semantic consistency essential for robotics and autonomous driving.
approach: 3DPoV employs self-supervised learning with temporal nearest-neighbor consistency loss across video frames, reference-guided ordering for consistent patch alignment, and a mixture of video datasets tailored to these objectives.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on keypoint matching under viewpoint variation and improves diverse backbones including DINOv3 on depth and surface normal estimation.

problem: Anonymous multi-agent path finding faces exponential scaling challenges in standard optimization formulations, requiring efficient solution methods for real-world robotics problems.
approach: Casts MAPF as multi-marginal optimal transport with Markovian structure that collapses to a polynomial-sized LP, then introduces Schrödinger bridges for entropic regularization enabling iterative Sinkhorn-type solution for large-scale problems.
contribution: Demonstrates optimality and scalability via Schrödinger bridge formulation that achieves near-optimal integral solutions at significant computational reduction.

problem: Diffusion Policy excels at modeling multi-modal action distributions but its multi-step denoising makes real-time visuomotor control impractical, and existing caching methods fail to adapt to robot-environment dynamics.
approach: Sparse ActionGen introduces rollout-adaptive prune-then-reuse mechanism identifying prunable computations and reusing cached activations, with observation-conditioned diffusion pruner for environment-aware adaptation and zig-zag activation reuse across timesteps and blocks.
contribution: Achieves up to 4× generation speedup on multiple robotic benchmarks without sacrificing performance.

problem: ESG rating and responsible investing require modeling high-dimensional multi-modal time series spanning ESG risks, financial returns, and sentiment, but existing solutions cannot jointly reason over heterogeneous numerical signals.
approach: A domain-aware representation learning framework uses value-aware tokens with block-wise orthogonal embeddings and FACET tokens for trajectory-level structure, training with geometry-preserving loss to forecast values and organize entities.
contribution: Enables accurate ESG forecasting, trajectory-based entity grouping, and latent-space search for superior asset selection and portfolio applications.

problem: Existing multi-agent systems rely on manually crafted agent roles and natural language communication, leading to task-specificity, limited reusability, and error accumulation in long-context multi-stage interactions.
approach: Agent Primitives proposes three reusable latent building blocks (Review, Voting and Selection, Planning and Execution) communicating via KV cache, with automatic system construction via an Organizer agent selecting primitives guided by a knowledge pool of successful configurations.
contribution: Improves accuracy by 12.0-16.5% over single-agent baselines while reducing token usage and latency by 3×-4× compared to text-based MAS.

problem: Foundation model-driven agents struggle with long-horizon planning due to transient reasoning, and existing skill induction methods fail to capture conditional logic needed for robust dynamic environment execution.
approach: Neuro-Symbolic Skill Induction lifts interaction traces into modular logic-grounded programs by synthesizing explicit control flows and dynamic variable binding, empowering agents to discover when and why to act.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines enabling agents to efficiently generalize from few-shot examples and flexibly adapt to unseen goals.

problem: Reliable uncertainty quantification on frozen GNNs requires expensive multi-pass sampling or retraining with auxiliary models to obtain evidential semantics.
approach: X-EviProbe constructs class-wise Dirichlet evidence by probing frozen latent space and native outputs, incorporating graph structure via lightweight evidence-strength propagation without retraining or additional components.
contribution: Achieves up to 33.4% AUROC improvement for OOD detection and 8.7% for misclassification detection, ranking among top methods without parameter tuning.

problem: Evaluating AI reviewers is challenging because existing metrics favor overlap with human reviews despite humans often covering only partial issues and making mistakes.
approach: CoCoReviewBench builds category-specific subsets and uses reviewer-author-meta-review discussions as expert annotations while filtering unreliable reviews to strengthen both completeness and correctness in evaluation.
contribution: Curates 3,900 ICLR and NeurIPS papers showing AI reviewers remain limited in correctness and prone to hallucinations, with reasoning models as more effective reviewers.

problem: LLMs can optimize intermediate representations in compilers but lack rigorous evaluation on whether they understand IR and can rewrite it under compiler-grade semantic constraints with meaningful performance gains.
approach: CIRBench provides 800 curated IR instances across four compiler tracks (Analysis, Repair, Refactor, Transform) with verifier, equivalence checking, and end-to-end performance measurement in unified layered correctness-aware evaluation.
contribution: Shows current LLMs fail on many IR tasks and underperform compiler baseline on median, but observe maximum speedup of 4.96× over -O3.

problem: Monolithic robotic manipulation policies conflate heterogeneous regimes of coarse relocation and contact-critical interaction, limiting manipulation skill development.
approach: Move-Then-Operate decouples manipulation into two phases via dual-expert policy routed by learnable phase selector, with phase labels automatically generated via MLLM-based pipeline from contextual cues like end-effector velocity.
contribution: Achieves 68.9% average success rate on RoboTwin2 benchmark, outperforming monolithic baseline by 24% and matching models trained on 10× more data.

problem: Sparse MoE models require entire model in memory despite few experts activating per token, and existing expert pruning ignores complex inter-dependencies between experts.
approach: SCHUR-A* formulates post-training MoE pruning as reconstruction-driven subset selection, using A* search with Schur-complement-based admissible heuristic upper bound for globally optimal expert selection within each layer.
contribution: Significantly outperforms greedy and ranking-based baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B, maintaining comparable performance under aggressive pruning.

problem: Microcanonical Langevin Monte Carlo shows strong inference performance but requires full-dataset gradients, making it prohibitively expensive for large-scale Bayesian deep learning problems.
approach: Studies whether microcanonical dynamics can leverage mini-batch gradient noise via continuous-time theoretical analysis, identifying critical failure modes (anisotropic gradient noise bias and numerical instabilities) and proposing gradient noise preconditioning plus energy-variance-based adaptive tuner.
contribution: Develops robust scalable microcanonical Monte Carlo sampler achieving state-of-the-art on high-dimensional inference tasks like Bayesian neural networks.

problem: Token pruning accelerates VLMs but its safety implications are underexplored, and pruning strategies may introduce vulnerabilities through Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification.
approach: Identifies Pruning-Induced Malicious Amplification mechanism where background token removal forces attention onto retained malicious anchors, proposes Safety-Aware Pruning that identifies malicious anchors, restores benign tokens, and reallocates attention.
contribution: Reduces Attack Success Rate by up to 62% without compromising efficiency or utility across three safety and four utility benchmarks.

problem: In-context tool calling incorporates detailed documentation into context causing substantial inference overhead and hallucination risks, while tuning methods fail to internalize specific tool details.
approach: ParaTool projects each tool into dedicated loadable parameters via three stages: parametric tool pre-training, soft tool selection with gating network, and parametric fine-tuning jointly updating tool parameters.
contribution: Significantly outperforms ICL-based baselines on Stable ToolBench and BFCL achieving superior performance while reducing computational complexity.

problem: Multi-task linear regression with contaminated tasks typically requires minimum eigenvalue bounds on task covariances, but these bounds fail in high-dimensional scenarios where prior guarantees become vacuous.
approach: Proposes matrix-weighted norm regularization estimator with relative balancedness condition quantifying each task's second moment relative to average inlier geometry, relaxing taskwise second-moment lower bounds.
contribution: In favorable regimes with moderate balancedness matches minimax optimal MSE rates under substantially weaker spectral assumptions with safety guarantee.

problem: Contrastive learning's conditions for recovering meaningful latent geometry remain incompletely understood, particularly how sampling diversity and encoder inductive bias interact.
approach: Develops measure-theoretic framework formalizing the diversity condition as support requirement on positive-pair sampling, showing full-support von Mises-Fisher implies latent recovery up to orthogonal transformation, introducing support-corrected InfoNCE variant.
contribution: Clarifies how sampling mechanisms and encoder inductive bias interact in contrastive learning through synthetic validation and CIFAR-10 experiments.

problem: Neural operators for dynamical systems exhibit spectral bias attenuating high-frequency components encoding small-scale structure, particularly damaging for weather forecasting where misrepresented high frequencies induce long-horizon instability.
approach: Multi-Scale Wavelet Transformers learn system dynamics in tokenized wavelet domain using wavelet-preserving downsampling retaining high-frequency features and wavelet-based attention capturing cross-scale dependencies.
contribution: Shows substantial error reductions and improved long-horizon spectral fidelity on chaotic systems, further reducing climatological bias on ERA5 climate reanalysis.

problem: Dominant video reasoning pipelines either plateau at model knowledge or require careful regularization with bounded context, limiting accuracy on complex multi-modal reasoning tasks.
approach: Uses frozen tool-integrated teacher to identify missing spatiotemporal dependencies and provide minimal evidence patches from original video, training student with chosen-rollout GRPO scheme and Robust Improvement Reward aligning optimization with outcome validity and dependency alignment.
contribution: Shows consistent accuracy gains and strong generalization across benchmarks via context repair approach minimizing training stack changes.

problem: MoE deployment is limited by high memory overhead storing all expert parameters as the number of experts increases, and existing merging methods suffer notable performance drop due to coarse-grained operations.
approach: PuzzleMoE performs sparse expert merging via element-wise weight redundancy identification with dual-mask approach capturing shared and expert-specific salient parameters, introducing bit-packed encoding reusing exponent bits for efficient inference.
contribution: Outperforms prior compression methods by up to 16.7% on MMLU at 50% compression ratio and achieves up to 1.80× end-to-end inference throughput gain.

problem: LLM fine-tuning remains bottlenecked by significant memory and computational demands despite parameter-efficient methods, with opportunities for selective backward computation.
approach: TokenDrop uses token-level importance-aware backpropagation skipping based on residual update magnitude during forward pass, introducing cumulative selection preserving gradient continuity and lazy scheduling deferring selection for globally informed scoring.
contribution: Achieves up to 42.9% memory reduction and up to 1.50× training speedup while preserving accuracy and outperforming existing backpropagation-skipping baselines.

problem: Video generation with Diffusion Transformers remains constrained by quadratic attention complexity, and existing sparse attention methods rely on oversimplified static patterns or expensive sampling, degrading quality.
approach: MOD-DiT uses Mixture-of-Distribution sampling-free dynamic attention framework with two-stage process: leveraging early denoising priors via distributed mixing for efficient linear approximation, then online block masking applying predicted masks with historical sparsity.
contribution: Achieves consistent acceleration and quality improvements across benchmarks and architectures for efficient high-quality video generation without sampling overhead.

problem: Existing debiasing methods suppress biased behavior but are brittle, weakly generalizable, data-inefficient, and prone to degrading general capability of LLMs.
approach: KnowBias identifies neurons encoding bias knowledge via attribution-based analysis on small bias-knowledge question sets, selectively enhancing them at inference time rather than suppressing.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art debiasing with minimal utility degradation, generalizing across bias types with data-efficient lightweight framework requiring no retraining.

problem: Early exit methods rely on output confidence as proxy for internal convergence, but don't directly examine when hidden state refinement truly completes.
approach: Examines geometry of hidden state trajectory discovering two-phase structure (large volatile early updates, small aligned later updates), tracking normalized update norm and cosine similarity with O(d) overhead, exiting when both indicate convergence.
contribution: Reduces FLOPs by 30-35% while retaining over 98% accuracy on LLaMA-2 models across QA and reasoning tasks.

problem: Graph prompting adapts frozen GNN encoders by modifying input structure, but existing approaches optimize continuous adjacency at training time with hard discretization at inference, causing train-test mismatch.
approach: DiP-G directly learns task-specific topology prompts in combinatorial space using perturbed Top-k solver on multi-hop local subgraphs, optimizing discrete structures via I-MLE gradient estimator with adaptive active-set screening.
contribution: Maintains scalability and accuracy while avoiding train-test mismatch through discrete prompting on few-shot datasets.

problem: Recovering latent order from noisy one-dimensional curve samples in high dimensions requires handling local geometric information while dealing with tangent direction sign ambiguity.
approach: STAGE estimates local tangent directions via neighborhood PCA, resolves sign ambiguity through graph-wide Z_2 synchronization, constructs signed local displacements by projecting onto oriented tangents, integrating into global scalar embedding via inhomogeneous least-squares.
contribution: Provides finite-sample Kendall's τ recovery bound explicit in curvature, noise, and sampling density, with accurate fast order recovery on synthetic curves and meaningful pseudotime on single-cell RNA-seq.
